script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: No. The tutor will explain which book to get, and the first lesson uses printed sheets.

script.speaker: Visitor
script.text: Good. I will register today and bring a notebook.

questions.prompt: How long does the Spanish course last?
questions.explanation_zh_hk: 西班牙語課程為期六星期。

questions.prompt: What will the class use in the first lesson?
questions.explanation_zh_hk: 第一堂會使用印好的講義。

questions.prompt: What will the visitor do today?
questions.explanation_zh_hk: 訪客表示今天會報名。

script.speaker: Ruth
script.text: I copied almost every sentence from the reading, but I still cannot explain its argument.

script.speaker: Khalid
script.text: Perhaps try writing the author’s claim in one sentence, then note the evidence separately.

script.speaker: Ruth
script.text: Would that mean leaving out the examples?

script.speaker: Khalid
script.text: Not necessarily. Keep one that illustrates the reasoning, rather than listing them all.

script.speaker: Ruth
script.text: I will try that before the seminar and see whether I can explain it without looking.

script.speaker: Khalid
script.text: And if you get stuck, mark the gap rather than copying more sentences. That will give you a specific question to raise in the discussion.

questions.prompt: What difficulty does Ruth describe?

options.text: She has summarised the argument but disagrees with it
She cannot explain the argument despite extensive notes
She understands the argument but cannot locate supporting examples

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Ruth 雖然抄了很多筆記，仍無法解釋文章論點。

questions.prompt: How does Khalid suggest organising the notes?

options.text: Separate the main claim from its evidence
Keep every example in the order it appears
Replace the author’s claim with a personal opinion

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Khalid 建議分開記錄主要論點和證據，而非逐句抄寫。

questions.prompt: What does Khalid’s final advice imply about gaps in understanding?

options.text: They should be hidden by adding longer quotations
They show that the reading should be abandoned
They can guide useful seminar questions

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Khalid 建議標記卡住的位置，再在討論中提問；不理解之處可幫助找出值得問的問題。

script.speaker: Maya
script.text: Our group wants to divide the report into four independent pieces.

script.speaker: Lewis
script.text: That could save time, but the sections may repeat one another.

script.speaker: Maya
script.text: Shall we agree on an outline first and assign someone to check the whole draft?

script.speaker: Lewis
script.text: Yes. We should also exchange drafts early enough to make changes.

script.speaker: Maya
script.text: I will suggest a shared deadline a week before submission.

script.speaker: Lewis
script.text: That should help, as long as checking the whole draft is a shared responsibility. One editor cannot resolve contradictions without the section writers explaining their evidence.

questions.prompt: What risk does Lewis identify?

options.text: The report will have too few authors

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Lewis 擔心各部分內容可能重複。

questions.prompt: What does Maya propose before dividing the work?
questions.explanation_zh_hk: Maya 建議先訂好大綱。

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the earlier deadline?

options.text: To prevent anyone reading another section
To leave time for review and changes

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 提早交草稿能預留互相檢視和修改的時間。

script.speaker: Imogen
script.text: I enjoy history, but I am considering the data module because it might help my dissertation.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Have you looked at how it is assessed?

script.speaker: Imogen
script.text: Yes, there is a practical project rather than a final examination, which appeals to me.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Then speak to last year’s students about the workload before deciding.

script.speaker: Imogen
script.text: Good idea. Enjoyment and usefulness both matter, but I need a realistic picture of the time involved.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Exactly. A module can be valuable without being the right choice this term, especially while you are planning your dissertation research.

questions.prompt: Why is Imogen considering data?

options.text: It covers the same material as her history module
It requires less work than every other module

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Imogen 認為數據科目可能有助撰寫論文；對話沒有說它最輕鬆。

questions.prompt: What appeals to her about assessment?

options.text: Students choose between a project and an examination
A practical project replaces a final examination
The project is optional rather than assessed

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 她喜歡以實作項目取代期末考試的安排，並非可自行選擇兩者。

questions.prompt: What is the tutor’s overall position?

options.text: Usefulness should be weighed against current commitments
A useful module is always worth taking immediately
Enjoyment matters more than any practical consideration

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 導師肯定科目的價值，但提醒她考慮本學期的時間和論文研究安排。

script.speaker: Nadia
script.text: We spent yesterday testing each other on definitions, but I still struggle to apply them.

script.speaker: Elliot
script.text: Then let us invent examples and explain which concept fits each one.

script.speaker: Nadia
script.text: What if we choose different concepts for the same example?

script.speaker: Elliot
script.text: That is useful: we can compare our reasons and check the course notes.

script.speaker: Nadia
script.text: I like that better than simply repeating the correct definition.

script.speaker: Elliot
script.text: We should still check the definitions when necessary. The aim is to use them accurately, not to treat every interpretation as equally convincing.

questions.prompt: What does Nadia still find difficult?
questions.explanation_zh_hk: Nadia 仍然難以運用定義。

questions.prompt: What will the pair do if they disagree?

options.text: Compare reasons and consult their notes
Assume both answers must be wrong

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 他們會比較理由，並查閱課程筆記。

questions.prompt: What does Elliot regard disagreement as?

options.text: Proof that revision together is pointless
A reason to memorise without examples
A chance to examine their reasoning

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Elliot 認為分歧有助檢視推理。

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: The lecture recording will be available tomorrow, although the discussion was not recorded.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: I missed the class. Could I rely on the recording for everything?

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: It covers the slides, but classmates raised useful objections afterwards.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: I will ask someone for their notes on that discussion.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Please do, and bring any remaining questions to my office hour.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: So the recording gives me a starting point, but I should combine it with the discussion notes before deciding what I still need to ask.

questions.prompt: What is missing from the recording?

options.text: The lecturer’s explanation of the slides

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 錄影沒有包含課後討論；它仍涵蓋投影片內容。

questions.prompt: Why does the lecturer mention objections?

options.text: They showed that the slides had been recorded incorrectly
They replaced the need to study the slides
They contributed useful material beyond the recording

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 同學提出的反對意見提供了錄影以外的有用內容。

questions.prompt: What conclusion does the student reach about catching up?

options.text: The office hour should replace reviewing the material
Several sources should be combined before seeking clarification
The recording makes classmates’ notes unnecessary

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 學生認為應先結合錄影與討論筆記，再確定仍有甚麼疑問。

script.speaker: Aisha
script.text: My feedback says my essay describes the sources well but needs more analysis.

script.speaker: Ben
script.text: Did you explain how the authors’ views relate to your own question?

script.speaker: Aisha
script.text: Not much. I mostly summarised each author in a separate paragraph.

script.speaker: Ben
script.text: Perhaps compare their claims and explain which evidence is more convincing and why.

script.speaker: Aisha
script.text: That gives me a clearer direction for the next draft.

script.speaker: Ben
script.text: You may not need more sources. Using the ones you already have to support a clear judgement could be more effective than adding another descriptive paragraph.

questions.prompt: What does the feedback say is missing?
questions.explanation_zh_hk: 評語指出文章需要更多分析。

questions.prompt: How did Aisha organise the essay?

options.text: She compared all authors in one table

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Aisha 主要逐段概述不同作者。

questions.prompt: What would Ben add?

options.text: A reasoned comparison of claims and evidence

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Ben 建議比較觀點及證據，並解釋判斷理由。

script.speaker: Hana
script.text: I am visiting Mei’s family for the first time. Should I take my shoes off at the door?

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Their household usually does, although customs differ even within the same community.

script.speaker: Hana
script.text: I will look for a clue when I arrive and ask if I am unsure.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: That makes sense. They may offer slippers, but you do not need to assume they will.

script.speaker: Hana
script.text: I will wear presentable socks just in case.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: And remember that asking politely gives them a chance to explain their own preference. A general guide to customs cannot tell you what every family expects.

questions.prompt: What does Tom say about the practice?

options.text: It is identical in every household

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Tom 指即使同一社群，不同家庭的做法也可能不同。

questions.prompt: What will Hana do if uncertain?

options.text: Keep her shoes on without checking

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Hana 說不肯定時會詢問主人家。

questions.prompt: Why will she choose presentable socks?

options.text: She plans to give them as a gift
She may need to remove her shoes

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 她可能需要脫鞋，所以會穿得體的襪子。

script.speaker: Farah
script.text: My neighbour invited me to a celebration, but I have never attended one like it.

script.speaker: Jon
script.text: You could ask whether there is a dress code or anything guests usually bring.

script.speaker: Farah
script.text: Would asking sound rude?

script.speaker: Jon
script.text: I think showing interest is better than pretending you already know. People’s preferences differ.

script.speaker: Farah
script.text: I will thank her for inviting me and ask what would be helpful.

script.speaker: Jon
script.text: You could mention that you are unfamiliar with the occasion. That explains the question without suggesting that she has to speak for a whole community.

questions.prompt: What is Farah unsure about?

options.text: What is appropriate at the celebration

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Farah 不熟悉這類慶祝活動的習慣。

questions.prompt: What does Jon suggest asking?

options.text: Whether the celebration can be cancelled
About clothing and anything guests might bring

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Jon 建議詢問衣著要求及應否帶東西。

questions.prompt: What principle underlies Jon’s advice?

options.text: Guests should never ask hosts for guidance
Respectful questions are preferable to assumptions

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Jon 認為有禮地詢問比假裝知道更好。

script.speaker: Priya
script.text: At our family meals, dishes are usually placed in the middle for everyone to share.

script.speaker: Oscar
script.text: I was about to serve myself a large portion straight away.

script.speaker: Priya
script.text: You can always take more later; leaving enough for others is appreciated.

script.speaker: Oscar
script.text: Thanks for explaining. Is it all right to ask what is in a dish?

script.speaker: Priya
script.text: Of course, especially if you need to avoid an ingredient.

script.speaker: Oscar
script.text: That is reassuring. I had mistaken taking a generous portion for showing appreciation, but here I can show it by leaving others a fair share.

questions.prompt: How are dishes generally served?

options.text: As individual portions chosen by the host
As a separate course for each guest

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 食物通常放在中央供大家分享。

questions.prompt: Why does Priya suggest a modest first helping?

options.text: The host expects guests to eat very little

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 先取適量可讓其他人也有足夠食物；她明確說可以稍後再取。

questions.prompt: What does Oscar reconsider?

options.text: How to express appreciation appropriately at this meal
Whether asking about ingredients is ever acceptable
Whether shared meals prevent people eating enough

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Oscar 原以為多取食物是欣賞，但得知在這個場合留足份量給別人也能表達尊重。

script.speaker: Zara
script.text: I am meeting our new colleague tomorrow and wondered whether to offer a handshake.

script.speaker: Colin
script.text: You could greet them verbally first and follow their lead.

script.speaker: Zara
script.text: I do not want to make them uncomfortable by guessing.

script.speaker: Colin
script.text: Exactly. People have different personal preferences, even when they share a background.

script.speaker: Zara
script.text: I will introduce myself and give them space to choose.

script.speaker: Colin
script.text: That should work. Being welcoming is about making the other person comfortable, rather than demonstrating that you know a rule you believe applies to their background.

questions.prompt: What does Colin suggest first?

options.text: Waiting for someone else to introduce Zara

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Colin 建議先用說話打招呼，再按對方反應行事。

questions.prompt: Why should Zara avoid assumptions?

options.text: A shared background determines everyone’s preference
A verbal greeting is compulsory in every workplace

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 即使背景相同，個人對打招呼方式的喜好仍可不同。

questions.prompt: What does Colin regard as the priority?

options.text: Showing knowledge of a presumed cultural rule
Ensuring every colleague greets people identically
Helping the new colleague feel comfortable

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Colin 強調應令對方自在，而非套用自己以為適用於某背景的規則。

script.speaker: Lucy
script.text: The invitation says seven. Should we arrive earlier to help?

script.speaker: Mateo
script.text: The host told me she will still be preparing then, so seven would be better.

script.speaker: Lucy
script.text: If the train is late, I will send her a message.

script.speaker: Mateo
script.text: Good. Expectations about timing vary, but her preference is clear here.

script.speaker: Lucy
script.text: Then we can offer to help once we arrive rather than turning up early.

script.speaker: Mateo
script.text: Yes. Help is only helpful if it fits what she needs. Arriving before she is ready might give her another person to look after while she is cooking.

questions.prompt: Why should they avoid arriving early?

options.text: The host will still be preparing
The train only runs after seven
Dinner has been moved to another day

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 主人家在七時前仍在準備。

questions.prompt: What will Lucy do if delayed?

options.text: Ask Mateo to change the invitation

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Lucy 若遲到會通知主人家。

questions.prompt: What guides their decision about arrival?

options.text: The guests’ wish to avoid helping
A rule that applies to every dinner

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 他們按這位主人家表明的意願決定時間。

script.speaker: Chair
script.text: We would like to thank you publicly at the community event.

script.speaker: Volunteer
script.text: That is kind, but I would rather not go on stage.

script.speaker: Chair
script.text: Would a note in the programme be comfortable, or would you prefer no mention?

script.speaker: Volunteer
script.text: A short note is fine. I am happy to help, just not keen on a public speech.

script.speaker: Chair
script.text: We will respect that and check the wording with you first.

script.speaker: Volunteer
script.text: Thank you. I would also like the note to mention the whole team, since the project depended on many people whose work was less visible.

questions.prompt: What does the volunteer decline?
questions.explanation_zh_hk: 義工不想上台，但接受簡短的書面鳴謝。

questions.prompt: Which alternative does the volunteer accept?

options.text: A programme entry written without consultation
A short speech delivered by the volunteer

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 義工接受場刊上的簡短鳴謝，主席亦答應先確認措辭。

questions.prompt: What does the volunteer’s final request suggest?

options.text: Recognition should reflect the collective effort
Only people seen at the event deserve credit
The chair should receive all the credit

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 義工要求同時提及整個團隊，因為項目依靠多人，包括較少曝光的成員。

script.speaker: Resident
script.text: The village bus runs only twice a day, which makes appointments difficult.

script.speaker: Councillor
script.text: A full hourly service may be too expensive for the number of passengers.

script.speaker: Resident
script.text: Could we try an extra journey on market day and record how many people use it?

script.speaker: Councillor
script.text: That would give us evidence, provided the timetable lets people reach their clinic appointments.

script.speaker: Resident
script.text: I will ask the operator for costs and possible connection times.

script.speaker: Councillor
script.text: Please do. Counting passengers would be useful, but we should also ask whether the trial lets people complete their appointments and get home on the same day.

questions.prompt: What problem does the resident raise?

options.text: The clinic has stopped offering appointments
The bus route avoids the village entirely

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 居民指出巴士每天只有兩班，令赴約不便。

questions.prompt: What trial is proposed?

options.text: An hourly service throughout the week
A replacement for every existing journey

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 居民建議在墟日加開一班作試行，並非立即開辦全週每小時一班。

questions.prompt: How does the councillor suggest judging the trial?

options.text: Treat passenger numbers as the only relevant evidence
Judge it solely by the operator’s quoted price
Consider useful return journeys as well as passenger numbers

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 議員除了要求點算乘客，也關注居民能否完成診症並即日回家，因此要衡量實際用途。

script.speaker: Amira
script.text: The council proposes closing our street to through traffic during school hours.

script.speaker: Joel
script.text: I like the idea of safer crossings, but deliveries still need access.

script.speaker: Amira
script.text: The draft allows access for residents and delivery vehicles.

script.speaker: Joel
script.text: Then I would support a trial, provided neighbouring streets are monitored too.

script.speaker: Amira
script.text: Yes, shifting congestion elsewhere would not solve the problem.

script.speaker: Joel
script.text: We should compare traffic counts before and during the trial, then adjust the hours or access arrangements if the evidence shows new problems on those streets.

questions.prompt: What benefit does Joel see?
questions.explanation_zh_hk: Joel 認為過路會更安全。

questions.prompt: Who retains access under the draft?
questions.explanation_zh_hk: 草案容許居民及送貨車輛進出。

questions.prompt: Why monitor neighbouring streets?
questions.explanation_zh_hk: 鄰近街道可能承受轉移的車流。

script.speaker: Caretaker
script.text: The hall is empty most weekday mornings, but its heating is expensive.

script.speaker: Resident
script.text: Could local groups share one morning instead of opening it for separate sessions?

script.speaker: Caretaker
script.text: Possibly, if they agree on noise and storage arrangements.

script.speaker: Resident
script.text: I will speak to the craft group and the language class about a joint timetable.

script.speaker: Caretaker
script.text: If both agree, we can estimate whether sharing actually saves money.

script.speaker: Resident
script.text: And ask whether the arrangement still suits their activities. A cheaper timetable would be little use if either group could no longer run its sessions properly.

questions.prompt: What expense concerns the caretaker?
questions.explanation_zh_hk: 管理員擔心暖氣費用。

questions.prompt: What must the groups agree on?

options.text: A common subject for both classes

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 團體須就噪音和儲物安排達成共識。

questions.prompt: What reservation does the resident express at the end?

options.text: Savings must not prevent the groups working effectively
The groups should share even if their activities become impractical
Financial savings are impossible in a shared building

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 居民提醒，即使省錢，安排仍須讓兩個團體正常運作；否則便失去意義。

script.speaker: Ravi
script.text: The flat near the station costs more than the one on the edge of town.

script.speaker: Ella
script.text: But I could walk to work from there and might not need a car.

script.speaker: Ravi
script.text: Have you included the cost of occasional train trips in your calculation?

script.speaker: Ella
script.text: Not yet. I should compare total monthly costs rather than rent alone.

script.speaker: Ravi
script.text: And visit both places in the evening to judge the noise.

script.speaker: Ella
script.text: I will. If the saving on transport offsets the higher rent, the central flat may be affordable, but I would still want to know whether I could sleep there.

questions.prompt: What advantage does the station flat offer Ella?

options.text: Train fares are included in its rent
Its rent is lower than the other flat’s

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Ella 可步行上班，或可不用養車，但租金本身較高。

questions.prompt: What has Ella not yet included?

options.text: Whether she could walk to work

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 她尚未計算偶爾乘火車的費用。

questions.prompt: What is Ella’s final position?

options.text: Lower transport costs would settle the decision by themselves
The cheaper rent makes the outer flat the only sensible choice
The total cost and evening noise both need checking

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Ella 會比較租金加交通的總成本，但即使負擔得起，仍要考慮晚上能否安睡。

script.speaker: Gardener
script.text: The park path will close for repairs for three weeks, starting Monday.

script.speaker: Resident
script.text: Will wheelchair users still be able to reach the pond?

script.speaker: Gardener
script.text: Yes, the eastern entrance remains open and has a level route to it.

script.speaker: Resident
script.text: Could you put that detail on the notice? The map currently only shows the closure.

script.speaker: Gardener
script.text: Certainly. I will add the accessible route before the weekend.

script.speaker: Resident
script.text: Thank you. Without that information, people might assume the whole pond area is inaccessible and decide not to visit, even though a suitable route is available.

questions.prompt: Why is the path closing?
questions.explanation_zh_hk: 小徑因維修而暫停開放，並非整個公園關閉。

questions.prompt: How can wheelchair users reach the pond?

options.text: Enter from the eastern side and cross the closed path
Use the main path after the repair team finishes each day
Use the level route from the eastern entrance

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 東面入口有平坦路線通往池塘，不需要經過封閉的小徑。

questions.prompt: Why does the resident want a more detailed notice?

options.text: The closure dates have already changed
An incomplete notice could discourage visits unnecessarily
The alternative route is currently unsuitable for wheelchairs

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 居民擔心只有封路資料會令人誤以為不能到池塘，明明有可用路線卻放棄到訪。

script.speaker: Nia
script.text: The new evening market has made the square livelier, but some residents complain about noise.

script.speaker: Sam
script.text: Could the musicians finish earlier while food stalls stay open?

script.speaker: Nia
script.text: That might help, though stallholders say music attracts customers.

script.speaker: Sam
script.text: Perhaps measure noise and ask both residents and traders before changing the licence.

script.speaker: Nia
script.text: Agreed. A decision based on evidence would be fairer than guessing.

script.speaker: Sam
script.text: And if an earlier finish reduces the noise but harms trade, we may need a different arrangement, such as moving the musicians away from the nearest homes.

questions.prompt: What concern have residents raised?
questions.explanation_zh_hk: 居民投訴夜市噪音。

questions.prompt: Why might traders resist an early finish for music?

options.text: They want all food stalls to close

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 攤販認為音樂能吸引顧客。

questions.prompt: What do the speakers agree to seek?

options.text: Noise measurements and views from both groups

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 他們希望收集噪音數據，以及居民和商戶意見。

script.speaker: Grower
script.text: Our apple juice is pressed locally, but some apples come from an orchard across the county border.

script.speaker: Shopkeeper
script.text: Then the label should not suggest that every apple is grown in this village.

script.speaker: Grower
script.text: Agreed. We can name both orchards and explain where the pressing happens.

script.speaker: Shopkeeper
script.text: Customers may value the local work without being misled about the ingredients.

script.speaker: Grower
script.text: I will revise the wording before the next batch is bottled.

script.speaker: Shopkeeper
script.text: That should make the distinction clear: supporting local production does not require claiming that every stage and every ingredient comes from exactly the same place.

questions.prompt: Where is the juice pressed?

options.text: At the orchard across the county border

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 果汁在本地榨製，但部分蘋果來自郡界另一邊的果園。

questions.prompt: Why should the label change?

options.text: Not all the apples are grown in the village
None of the production happens locally
The pressing location changes with every bottle

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 並非所有蘋果都在村內種植，標籤不應令顧客產生這個印象。

questions.prompt: What distinction does the shopkeeper emphasise?

options.text: Local processing guarantees that all ingredients are local
Ingredients matter more than where the processing takes place
Local processing and local ingredients are separate claims

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 店主區分本地加工與本地原材料：果汁可在本地製造，但部分蘋果仍來自其他地方。

script.speaker: Baker
script.text: This loaf uses flour from the mill ten miles away, but the seeds are imported.

script.speaker: Customer
script.text: I appreciate knowing that. Is the flour always available?

script.speaker: Baker
script.text: Not always; after a poor harvest we may need another supplier.

script.speaker: Customer
script.text: Would you change the sign if that happened?

script.speaker: Baker
script.text: Yes, we update it whenever the source changes.

script.speaker: Customer
script.text: Then I would be comfortable buying it even when you use another supplier. Accurate information matters more to me than a local claim that cannot always be met.

questions.prompt: Which ingredient comes from the nearby mill?

options.text: Both the flour and the seeds

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 麵粉來自附近磨坊，種籽則是進口的。

questions.prompt: Why might the baker use another supplier?

options.text: The imported seeds cannot be used with local flour
The customer requests a different recipe
A poor harvest could limit supply

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 歉收可能令麵粉供應不足，才需要其他供應商。

questions.prompt: What does the customer value most?

options.text: Using the same supplier even when flour is unavailable
An honest account of changing sources
A permanent local label regardless of the source

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 顧客表示，即使供應商改變也可接受，最重視資料準確。

script.speaker: Maker
script.text: These cups are shaped in my workshop, but another studio fires them in its kiln.

script.speaker: Visitor
script.text: Does sharing the kiln affect when an order is ready?

script.speaker: Maker
script.text: Yes. I wait until several makers have enough work to fill it, which saves energy.

script.speaker: Visitor
script.text: So a custom order could take longer than an item already on the stall?

script.speaker: Maker
script.text: Exactly. I give each customer an estimated date before they order.

script.speaker: Visitor
script.text: I can allow a little extra time, then. I would rather know about the wait now than discover it after choosing a cup as a present for next weekend.

questions.prompt: Where are the cups fired?

options.text: At a kiln installed at the fair

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 杯子在製作者的工作室成形，再到另一間工作室燒製。

questions.prompt: Why do makers wait to fill the kiln?

options.text: To guarantee a fixed weekly completion date
To make all cups the same colour

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 多位製作者一起裝滿窯可節省能源，但可能影響完成時間。

questions.prompt: What does the visitor’s response imply?

options.text: Knowing the delay in advance makes planning possible
The visitor needs a custom cup by next weekend
An estimated date removes all uncertainty about completion

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 訪客願意預留時間，並指出若買作下週末的禮物，便應事前知道等待安排。

script.speaker: Farmer
script.text: The box contents change with the season, so we cannot promise tomatoes every week.

script.speaker: Subscriber
script.text: Could you publish a likely list beforehand? I plan meals for a large family.

script.speaker: Farmer
script.text: Yes, although weather may force a last-minute substitution.

script.speaker: Subscriber
script.text: A provisional list would still help as long as the possible changes are clear.

script.speaker: Farmer
script.text: We will email one on Monday and confirm any substitutions on collection day.

script.speaker: Subscriber
script.text: That is a reasonable compromise. I can plan around the likely contents and keep one meal flexible, rather than expecting the farm to guarantee what it cannot control.

questions.prompt: Why are tomatoes not guaranteed weekly?

options.text: The farm has stopped growing them permanently
Subscribers have already chosen other vegetables

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 農產品盒內容隨季節改變，並非永久停止供應番茄。

questions.prompt: Why does the subscriber want an early list?

options.text: To choose crops for the farmer to plant that week

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 訂戶需要為大家庭安排膳食。

questions.prompt: What does the subscriber accept in the final response?

options.text: An early list must be a guarantee of every item
Meal planning is impossible without fixed contents
Useful advance information can remain provisional

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 訂戶認為暫定清單仍有用，並可留一餐彈性調整，接受農場無法控制天氣。

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: The dairy offers tours, but production areas cannot be entered during cleaning.

script.speaker: Visitor
script.text: Does that mean the afternoon group sees less?

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: They view the process through a window and spend more time with the cheesemaker.

script.speaker: Visitor
script.text: That sounds different rather than necessarily worse.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: Exactly. The booking page explains both versions so visitors can choose.

script.speaker: Visitor
script.text: I would probably choose the afternoon, then. Asking the maker about decisions interests me more than standing beside the equipment, provided I can still see the process clearly.

questions.prompt: Why can visitors not enter the production area at certain times?

options.text: The afternoon group has not booked in advance
The cheesemaker only works in the morning

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 生產區清潔期間不能進入，並非下午完全沒有製作活動。

questions.prompt: How does the afternoon group observe production?

options.text: Through a recording made the previous day
By entering once the morning visitors leave

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 下午團可透過窗戶觀看製作過程。

questions.prompt: Why does the visitor lean towards the afternoon tour?

options.text: The visitor expects the process to finish before the tour
More discussion with the maker suits the visitor’s interests
The visitor thinks it includes more time beside the equipment

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 遊客較有興趣了解製作者的決定，所以更長的交流時間對他更有吸引力。

script.speaker: Grandmother
script.text: When I was young, a library van stopped near our farm every fortnight.

script.speaker: Leah
script.text: Did you borrow the same sort of books I do now?

script.speaker: Grandmother
script.text: Mostly adventure stories, though I remember the librarian recommending a book about stars.

script.speaker: Leah
script.text: Is that why you became interested in astronomy?

script.speaker: Grandmother
script.text: It helped, but watching the night sky with my brother mattered just as much.

script.speaker: Leah
script.text: So it was a mixture of reading and experience. I had imagined one book changing everything, but it sounds as though each made the other more interesting.

questions.prompt: How often did the van visit?
questions.explanation_zh_hk: 流動圖書館每兩星期來一次，即 every fortnight。

questions.prompt: Who recommended the book about stars?
questions.explanation_zh_hk: 圖書館員推薦了關於星星的書。

questions.prompt: What does Leah revise about her interpretation?

options.text: Several influences contributed rather than one decisive book
The book mattered more than Grandmother admits
Watching the sky happened before Grandmother learnt to read

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Leah 起初想像是一本書改變一切，後來接受閱讀與親身觀星共同引發興趣。

script.speaker: Noah
script.text: I remember Grandad making soup on Sundays, but I cannot recall what made it taste smoky.

script.speaker: Sister
script.text: He charred the peppers over a flame first. I wrote the recipe down when we visited him.

script.speaker: Noah
script.text: I thought he used smoked cheese.

script.speaker: Sister
script.text: That went on top sometimes, but the peppers were in every batch.

script.speaker: Noah
script.text: Let us try your notes and see whether the taste brings back the kitchen.

script.speaker: Sister
script.text: We can add the cheese afterwards if we want. That way we can tell whether the peppers produce the flavour you remember, instead of changing several things at once.

questions.prompt: What does Noah struggle to remember?

options.text: The source of the smoky taste

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Noah 記得星期日喝湯，但想不起煙燻味的來源。

questions.prompt: What was included in every batch?
questions.explanation_zh_hk: 每次都有用火烤至表面焦香的甜椒，煙燻芝士則只是有時加在上面。

questions.prompt: Why does the sister suggest adding cheese afterwards?

options.text: To prove that Grandad never used cheese
To avoid following the recorded recipe
To distinguish the peppers’ contribution to the remembered taste

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 先不加芝士可分辨甜椒本身是否帶出記憶中的味道，避免同時改變多個因素。

script.speaker: Daisy
script.text: I remember forgetting my line in the school play and everyone laughing.

script.speaker: Father
script.text: You paused, but your friend whispered the line and the audience applauded at the end.

script.speaker: Daisy
script.text: Perhaps I mixed up the laughter from the funny scene with my mistake.

script.speaker: Father
script.text: Memories can change. We still have the programme, though not a recording.

script.speaker: Daisy
script.text: I would like to see the programme; it might help me remember the other children.

script.speaker: Father
script.text: It should help with names, though it cannot tell us exactly when the audience laughed. We may have to accept that part will remain uncertain.

questions.prompt: How did Daisy’s friend help?

options.text: By turning the mistake into a funny scene
By bringing the play to an early end

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 朋友低聲提示了台詞，令 Daisy 可以繼續演出。

questions.prompt: What does Daisy reconsider?

options.text: Whether the performance had an audience
Whether her friend appeared in the play
Whether the laughter followed her mistake

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Daisy 重新思考笑聲是否因她出錯而起，可能其實來自搞笑場面。

questions.prompt: What limitation does Father identify in the programme?

options.text: It is less useful for names than for checking dialogue
It can identify participants but not establish the timing of laughter
It provides a full record of the audience’s reactions

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 父親指出場刊可幫助確認名字，卻不能證明觀眾何時發笑。

script.speaker: Hugo
script.text: I was certain you taught me to cycle in the park.

script.speaker: Aunt
script.text: I helped you practise there, but your mother first held the saddle in our street.

script.speaker: Hugo
script.text: That explains why I remember both places.

script.speaker: Aunt
script.text: You fell once in the park and wanted to stop, then tried again after a break.

script.speaker: Hugo
script.text: I had forgotten that part. It makes the memory less simple than I thought.

script.speaker: Aunt
script.text: Your memory of the park is still real; it just does not include the whole sequence. Remembering one important afternoon can make earlier lessons less noticeable.

questions.prompt: Where did Hugo first learn with help?
questions.explanation_zh_hk: 媽媽最初在街上扶着車座教他。

questions.prompt: What happened after Hugo fell?

options.text: He took a break and tried again

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 他休息後再嘗試。

questions.prompt: What does Hugo realise about his memory?

options.text: It combines events from different places

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 他發現記憶結合了不同地方發生的事。

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: You keep asking about the summer we stayed by the coast.

script.speaker: Theo
script.text: I remember collecting shells, but I do not remember the cottage.

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: It was a small caravan, actually, and rain kept us indoors for two days.

script.speaker: Theo
script.text: That is surprising. My memory is full of sunshine.

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: You may remember the beach most clearly because that was your favourite part.

script.speaker: Theo
script.text: That makes sense. The sunny moments are not invented, but perhaps I have let them stand for the whole holiday and forgotten the ordinary time indoors.

questions.prompt: Where did the family stay?
questions.explanation_zh_hk: 一家人住在小型拖車屋，並非 Theo 以為的鄉間小屋。

questions.prompt: What does Theo remember most clearly?
questions.explanation_zh_hk: Theo 清楚記得在海灘拾貝殼，卻不記得住宿情況。

questions.prompt: What conclusion does Theo reach?

options.text: Remembering sunshine proves that it did not rain
His beach memories must have been invented
A true but selective memory can give an incomplete picture

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Theo 認為晴天的片段是真的，但只記住喜愛的時刻，未能代表整段假期。

script.speaker: Resident
script.text: Can I put food waste in a plastic bag before placing it in the caddy?

script.speaker: Collector
script.text: Ordinary plastic bags cannot go in. Use a liner approved by the council or wrap the waste in newspaper.

script.speaker: Resident
script.text: The packaging on my liners says compostable. Is that enough?

script.speaker: Collector
script.text: Check the council’s current list, because not every compostable liner suits our processing system.

script.speaker: Resident
script.text: I will check before using the rest of the packet.

script.speaker: Collector
script.text: Thank you. A label can describe how a material breaks down under particular conditions without confirming that our collection service can process it. The local instructions are what matter here.

questions.prompt: Which wrapping is explicitly accepted by this service?
questions.explanation_zh_hk: 對話中的收集員明確表示這項服務接受報紙包裹。

questions.prompt: Why should the resident check the list?

options.text: Compostable liners have all been prohibited nationally
Approved liners and newspaper must be used together
Not all compostable liners suit the local system

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 並非所有可堆肥袋都適合對話中的當地處理系統。

questions.prompt: What distinction does the collector make?

options.text: Collection instructions apply only to unlabelled packaging
A material’s description does not guarantee local acceptance
Every compostable label confirms approval by every council

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 「可堆肥」描述物料在特定條件下的性質，不能保證某地的收集服務可以處理。

script.speaker: Teacher
script.text: Our class collected litter around the school gate and found many takeaway cups.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: Does that prove pupils dropped them?

script.speaker: Teacher
script.text: No. People walking past use the same pavement, so we cannot identify the source.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: We could count items at different times and ask local businesses about bin provision.

script.speaker: Teacher
script.text: That would give us a better basis for proposing a solution.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: And we could repeat the counts after any change. Otherwise a single tidy morning might look like success even if the amount of litter has not fallen overall.

questions.prompt: What did the class find frequently?

options.text: Food wrappers from the canteen only

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 學生發現很多外賣杯，但不能單憑地點確認是誰丟棄。

questions.prompt: Why can they not blame pupils?

options.text: The survey took place entirely outside term time
Other people use the same pavement
The cups have already been traced to local shops

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 其他途人也使用同一行人路，因此不能認定垃圾全由學生丟棄。

questions.prompt: Why does the student suggest repeating the counts?

options.text: To distinguish a lasting improvement from a temporary change
To ensure that the same pupils are blamed each time
To avoid comparing the situation before and after action

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 單一早上的整潔未必代表整體垃圾量下降，重複點算有助判斷改善是否持續。

script.speaker: Technician
script.text: Your lamp needs a new switch; the shade and wiring are still in good condition.

script.speaker: Customer
script.text: Would replacing the switch cost more than buying a new lamp?

script.speaker: Technician
script.text: The repair is slightly cheaper, and I can give you a written estimate before starting.

script.speaker: Customer
script.text: Please do. I would prefer to keep it if the total stays within that estimate.

script.speaker: Technician
script.text: I will contact you if I find any additional problem.

script.speaker: Customer
script.text: That is fine. Keeping a usable lamp appeals to me, but I am not agreeing to unlimited work. I would want to reconsider if a further repair made the total substantially higher.

questions.prompt: Which part needs replacement?
questions.explanation_zh_hk: 檯燈需要更換開關，燈罩和電線目前狀況良好。

questions.prompt: How does the initial repair price compare with a new lamp?
questions.explanation_zh_hk: 按目前估計，維修價格稍低於購買新燈；額外問題仍可能影響總價。

questions.prompt: What best describes the customer’s approval?

options.text: Permission to carry out any additional repair automatically
A refusal to reconsider even if the cost rises
Conditional on the scope and cost staying acceptable

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 顧客想保留可用的燈，但只接受合理範圍內的維修，若成本大幅增加便要重新考慮。

script.speaker: Organiser
script.text: The river clean-up is on Saturday, but volunteers should not enter the water.

script.speaker: Volunteer
script.text: What should we do if we find something sharp on the bank?

script.speaker: Organiser
script.text: Leave it in place and tell a team leader, who has the right equipment.

script.speaker: Volunteer
script.text: Will gloves and bags be supplied for ordinary litter?

script.speaker: Organiser
script.text: Yes, and we will explain the collection points at the briefing.

script.speaker: Volunteer
script.text: I will wait for those instructions, then. I had hoped to start early, but collecting more rubbish is not worth taking on a task we have not been equipped to do.

questions.prompt: Where should volunteers remain?
questions.explanation_zh_hk: 這次活動的義工不應進入水中，並沒有容許淺水的例外。

questions.prompt: How should they handle a sharp object?

options.text: Carry it to the collection point in an ordinary bag
Move it away before finding a leader
Leave it and notify a leader

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 按活動指示，尖銳物件應留在原處並通知有合適裝備的組長。

questions.prompt: What does the volunteer’s final response show?

options.text: An intention to begin early with the supplied gloves
A willingness to put the briefing before starting work
A belief that collecting more litter overrides the instructions

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 義工原想提早開始，但接受先聽指示，認為不應為多收垃圾而處理未獲裝備的工作。

script.speaker: Owner
script.text: We are considering bicycle deliveries for nearby orders.

script.speaker: Courier
script.text: That could reduce van journeys, though heavy parcels would still need another vehicle.

script.speaker: Owner
script.text: Would a trial during the busiest two hours show whether it works?

script.speaker: Courier
script.text: It would show something, but include a quieter period too or the results may be misleading.

script.speaker: Owner
script.text: Agreed. We will record distances, delivery times and the weight of parcels.

script.speaker: Courier
script.text: Then we can identify which orders suit bicycles, rather than treating the trial as a choice between using them for everything or keeping every delivery in a van.

questions.prompt: What limitation does the courier identify?

options.text: Nearby journeys are unsuitable for bicycles
The trial cannot include any van deliveries
Heavy parcels may require another vehicle

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 較重的包裹可能仍需要其他車輛，並非所有訂單都適合單車。

questions.prompt: Why include a quiet period in the trial?

options.text: The busiest period has already proved successful
A busy period alone may give a misleading picture
Quiet periods eliminate the need to measure distance

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 只測試繁忙時間，可能不能反映不同時段的整體情況。

questions.prompt: What outcome does the courier favour?

options.text: Selecting suitable orders using the trial evidence
Replacing every van delivery regardless of parcel weight
Keeping all van journeys unless bicycles suit every order

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 速遞員希望按數據找出適合單車的訂單，而非把決定看成全部採用或全部放棄。

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Should all museums be free to enter?

script.speaker: Jules
script.text: Free entry removes one barrier, but museums still need funding to care for collections.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: How might they balance those concerns?

script.speaker: Jules
script.text: They could keep the permanent collection free and charge for some special exhibitions, while offering concessions.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: What would you check before recommending that policy?

script.speaker: Jules
script.text: Whether the charges exclude particular groups and whether the income covers the costs. If concessions still leave people unable to attend, I would want to reconsider how those exhibitions are funded.

questions.prompt: What benefit of free entry does Jules mention?

options.text: It makes concessions unnecessary at every exhibition
It removes the need for external funding

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 免費入場可消除其中一個參觀障礙，但博物館仍需要資金。

questions.prompt: What compromise does Jules suggest?

options.text: Free permanent collections with some paid exhibitions
Free special exhibitions funded by charging for the permanent collection
The same entrance charge for every visitor

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Jules 建議常設展覽免費，部分特展收費並提供優惠。

questions.prompt: What would make Jules reconsider the funding arrangement?

options.text: Some visitors choose only the free permanent collection
The exhibitions require care for their collections
Concessions still fail to make exhibitions accessible to some groups

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Jules 會檢查即使有優惠，是否仍有群體無法參觀，並可能因此重新考慮資金安排。

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Does working from home always improve productivity?

script.speaker: Mariam
script.text: Not always. It saves commuting time, but some people lack a quiet workspace.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Would you require everyone to return to an office?

script.speaker: Mariam
script.text: No. A mixture could work if teams agree when they need to meet in person.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: How could an employer assess that arrangement?

script.speaker: Mariam
script.text: Ask staff about its effects and compare outcomes over time, rather than assuming one pattern suits everyone. I would include the quality of collaboration as well as individual output, since quick results do not reveal every effect.

questions.prompt: What benefit does Mariam identify?

options.text: A quieter workspace for every employee
More opportunities for spontaneous office conversations

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 在家工作可省卻通勤時間，但並非人人家中都有安靜地方。

questions.prompt: What arrangement does she favour?

options.text: An identical home-working schedule for every team
Daily office attendance regardless of the work
A mixture with agreed in-person meetings

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 她建議混合安排，並按團隊需要商定何時見面。

questions.prompt: What does Mariam imply about measuring success?

options.text: One short-term increase in output proves the policy suits everyone
Individual output alone may overlook effects on collaboration
Staff opinions should replace every measure of work

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Mariam 提出同時觀察合作質素、個人成果與員工意見；單看短期產出不足以全面評估。

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Some people say failure is always valuable. Do you agree?

script.speaker: Alec
script.text: It can teach us something, but only if we examine what happened and have a chance to try again.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Can you give an example?

script.speaker: Alec
script.text: My first community event had poor attendance. We asked residents about the timing and changed it for the next one.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: So was the first event useful?

script.speaker: Alec
script.text: It was disappointing, but the feedback helped us improve; disappointment alone would not have done that. I would not call every failure valuable, because sometimes people lack either useful feedback or the resources to act on it.

questions.prompt: What condition does Alec attach to learning from failure?

options.text: Repeating the same action without reflection
Reflecting and having a chance to retry

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Alec 認為需要反思，並有機會再嘗試。

questions.prompt: What did the organisers change?

options.text: The location of the whole town
The timing of the next event

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 他們根據居民意見改變下次活動時間。

questions.prompt: What distinction does Alec make?

options.text: Feedback enabled improvement; disappointment alone did not
The first event had excellent attendance

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 他指出是回饋促成改善，單靠失望並不足夠。

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Who should decide what public art is installed in a town?

script.speaker: Mei
script.text: Artists bring expertise, but residents live with the result, so both should have a voice.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Could public voting alone settle it?

script.speaker: Mei
script.text: A vote may reveal preferences, but people also need information about cost and maintenance.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: What process would you suggest?

script.speaker: Mei
script.text: An open shortlist with clear budgets, followed by consultation and an explanation of the final decision. Not everyone will like the outcome, but they should be able to see how their views and the practical constraints were considered.

questions.prompt: Whose voices does Mei want included?
questions.explanation_zh_hk: Mei 認為藝術家的專業和居民的意見都應納入考慮。

questions.prompt: Why is a vote alone insufficient in her view?

options.text: People also need cost and maintenance information
The most popular design always costs the least
Residents cannot form any preferences about art

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 她認為投票前亦需了解成本和維修等資料。

questions.prompt: What does Mei want an explanation of the decision to achieve?

options.text: Guarantee that every resident will like the chosen work
Show that professional advice replaced public consultation
Make the reasoning visible even to people who disagree

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Mei 接受不可能人人喜歡結果，但公眾應能看見意見和實際限制如何影響決定。

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Should people always use their free time to learn a new skill?

script.speaker: Evan
script.text: Learning can be rewarding, but rest and unstructured time have value too.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Could rest be a waste of time?

script.speaker: Evan
script.text: Not if it helps someone recover or enjoy being with others, though individuals need different balances.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: How do you decide for yourself?

script.speaker: Evan

script.text: Our visitor left her umbrella here, and my father says returning it in person is the polite thing to do.

script.text: That could be kind, but she lives across town and may prefer us to bring it next time we meet.

script.speaker: Iris
script.text: Would asking make the gesture seem less generous?

script.speaker: Kareem
script.text: I do not think so. Offering both options lets her choose without creating an unexpected visit.

script.speaker: Iris
script.text: I will message her and say we are happy to drop it off if that is useful.

An unplanned visit may be inconvenient

Leave it outside the visitor’s home without warning

questions.prompt: What does Kareem think courtesy involves?

Following one rule regardless of the circumstances
Avoiding all direct communication with visitors

script.text: The association usually begins its anniversary with a long formal speech, but several newer members suggested a shorter welcome.

script.text: Could we keep a brief introduction and put the full history in a printed programme?

script.text: That seems a useful compromise, provided we ask the people who prepare the speech first.

script.speaker: Clara
script.text: We should also offer the programme online for anyone who cannot attend.

script.speaker: Imran
script.text: Yes. Changing a custom can preserve its purpose if the people involved help decide how.

questions.prompt: Why might some members want to retain the speech?

options.text: It is shorter than the introduction in the printed programme
It gives newer members an opportunity to lead the welcome

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Imran 指演講記錄團體歷史，故部分成員可能重視它。

questions.prompt: What compromise does Clara propose?

options.text: Give a shorter welcome and provide the full history separately
Remove the history from the event entirely
Replace the printed history with a longer formal speech

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Clara 建議縮短開場，並在節目單保留完整歷史。

questions.prompt: What does Imran consider necessary before changing the custom?

options.text: Asking only those who joined recently
Assuming that everyone values the same format
Consulting the people involved in preparing it

script.text: The invitation lists the whole household, but I am not certain whether that includes my cousin, who is staying for a month.

script.text: Rather than deciding for the hosts, you could explain the situation and ask if there is room.

script.text: I worry the question might make them feel obliged to invite her.

script.text: You can make it easy to decline by saying you understand if the numbers are fixed.

script.text: That sounds fair. I will check before telling my cousin she is included.

script.speaker: Beth
script.text: And if there is no space, it does not necessarily mean she is unwelcome personally.

questions.prompt: Why is the invitation ambiguous to Tariq?

His own name is missing from the invitation
The event date has not been announced

questions.prompt: How can he avoid putting pressure on the hosts?

options.text: Tell his cousin that a place is guaranteed
Ask the hosts to change the venue
Acknowledge that fixed numbers may prevent an extra guest

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Beth 建議表明理解名額可能固定，讓主人家可以婉拒。

A refusal may reflect limited capacity rather than personal dislike
The invitation to Tariq must also be cancelled

script.speaker: Mei
script.text: At the welcome table we usually offer tea straight away, but a visitor seemed unsure whether she could refuse.

script.text: Perhaps we should say that water is available too and that it is perfectly fine to take nothing.

script.text: Would listing choices make our greeting feel less warm?

script.text: Not if we say it naturally. It gives people room to respond according to their needs.

script.text: We could also label the drinks, since not everyone will recognise the ingredients.

script.speaker: Alec
script.text: That would make the custom easier to join without assuming that every guest has the same preferences.

options.text: She asked the organisers to remove every drink
She had brought a recipe for the table
She appeared uncertain about declining tea

questions.prompt: Why does Alec suggest offering alternatives?

To let guests choose without feeling pressured
To prevent anyone from accepting tea

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of labelling drinks?

options.text: To help guests make informed choices about ingredients
To require every guest to taste each drink
To replace the verbal welcome entirely

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 標示飲品可讓不認識材料的客人自行作出選擇。

script.text: My uncle remembers it as something the whole village did together.

script.speaker: Neil
script.text: He may mean it felt like a shared occasion. Could you present his memory alongside what the records show?

script.speaker: Sofia
script.text: Then I could write that it was a familiar local custom, with a separate quotation from him.

script.speaker: Neil

questions.prompt: How does Neil suggest using the uncle’s memory?

options.text: Present it as his experience alongside the archive evidence
Use it to correct every household entry in the archive
Remove it unless it agrees with every written record

questions.prompt: What does the revised wording achieve?

It replaces the archive with an account from one participant
It recognises the custom without overstating how widely it was practised

script.text: That would save some journeys, although one vehicle cannot provide every specialist service.

script.text: The proposal says it will visit twice a month and refer complicated cases to the town clinic.

script.text: I will suggest alternating weekdays when the council asks for feedback.

script.text: That would help them test whether the service is accessible in practice, not just close on a map.

questions.prompt: Why does Leah suggest alternating weekdays?

To ensure all referrals happen on Tuesdays
To make visits usable for people with different work patterns

A nearby service must also be available at suitable times
Distance is the only factor that matters

script.text: That could bring residents into the centre, but I wonder whether deliveries will block the narrow pavement.

script.speaker: Nadia
script.text: The drawings show a rear entrance, though the planning notice does not say when deliveries would happen.

script.text: We should ask for a delivery plan before deciding whether to support the application.

script.text: I like the idea of keeping a shop, so I do not want our concern to sound like automatic opposition.

script.text: Then say that clearly: we support the aim but need practical details about access.

questions.prompt: What benefit does Nadia see in the proposal?

options.text: The rear entrance would remove the need for any delivery restrictions
A grocery could remain in the village centre

The drawings do not establish how access will work at delivery times
They want to prevent any grocery from opening

Oppose the proposal without examining it
Promise that deliveries will never cause problems

script.text: Could the lights point downwards and switch on only when someone approaches?

script.speaker: Mo
script.text: Perhaps, but we would need to check whether the sensors work for cyclists and wheelchair users too.

script.text: I will ask for a trial on one section rather than assume the design solves everything.

Improving visibility while limiting disturbance to nearby homes
Keeping the path completely dark in order to preserve residents’ privacy

options.text: The proposed sensors need to work for a range of people
Only cyclists are allowed on the path
Wheelchair users have requested a road closure

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Mo 希望確認感應器對單車使用者和輪椅使用者都有效。

Avoid asking residents for their views
Gather different users’ observations before deciding on the design

The caretaker has forbidden electronic displays

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Elliot 接受反例，將原先絕對的說法修正為科技正常時可能節省交通時間。

questions.prompt: What response does he propose after a connection failure?

options.text: Make switching to another appointment format straightforward
Ask patients to repeat the same failed call indefinitely

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 他建議保留兩種方式，並在技術故障後方便轉換。

questions.prompt: What information would guide the balance of appointments?

options.text: The number of bookings alone, regardless of who can use each format
Only the preference of staff already working on online appointments
Demand, access needs and waiting times

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 他會考慮需求、使用需要及兩種方式的輪候時間。

script.speaker: Examiner
script.text: You suggested improving the town centre. What is one change you would make first?

script.speaker: Candidate
script.text: I would improve access to the square, especially for people travelling on foot.

script.speaker: Examiner
script.text: That is quite broad. Can you give a specific example?

script.speaker: Candidate
script.text: I would widen the crossing’s waiting area, where people currently gather beside the road.

script.speaker: Examiner
script.text: How would you judge whether it had worked?

script.speaker: Candidate
script.text: I would observe crowding at different busy times and ask local users, including people with pushchairs or wheelchairs, about their experience.

questions.prompt: Why does the examiner request an example?

options.text: The initial suggestion is too general to assess easily
The candidate has already provided a detailed cost
The square has been closed permanently

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 候選人最初只說改善通行，考官希望聽到具體做法。

questions.prompt: Which change does the candidate identify?

options.text: Removing all crossings from the square
Closing the town centre to pedestrians
Widening the waiting area at a crossing

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 候選人建議擴闊過路處的等候空間。

questions.prompt: What would the proposed evaluation combine?

options.text: Feedback only from people who designed the new crossing
Observations of crowding and feedback from varied users
Only a prediction made before the work

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 候選人建議在繁忙時間觀察擠迫情況，並徵詢不同使用者意見。

script.speaker: Organiser
script.text: Would you be able to lead the Saturday walk if the usual guide is away?

script.speaker: Volunteer
script.text: I could, provided someone familiar with the route joins me for the first section.

script.speaker: Organiser
script.text: We can ask Priya, but she may need to leave after half an hour.

script.speaker: Volunteer
script.text: That would be enough for the part I have not walked before. I know the rest of the route.

script.speaker: Organiser
script.text: Shall I confirm you as leader now?

script.speaker: Volunteer
script.text: Please check with Priya first. If she cannot come, we should find another guide rather than assume I can lead safely.

questions.prompt: What condition does the volunteer set?

options.text: Priya remains for the entire walk
The walk changes to a different day
A route-familiar person joins for the unfamiliar first section

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 義工願意帶隊的條件是熟悉路線的人陪同走過不熟悉的首段。

questions.prompt: Why might Priya’s half hour be sufficient?

options.text: The volunteer has never walked any of the route
It covers the section the volunteer does not know
It is the full duration of the walk

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 義工熟悉其餘路段，半小時可覆蓋不熟悉的部分。

questions.prompt: What is the best next response by the organiser?

options.text: Check whether Priya can join before confirming the volunteer
Announce the volunteer as leader without checking
Cancel Priya’s involvement and leave the route unchanged

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 義工明確要求先確認 Priya 能否同行，才決定是否帶隊。

script.speaker: Panel member
script.text: Your proposal costs more than the alternative. Why should the panel consider it?

script.speaker: Applicant
script.text: It includes training for local volunteers, while the cheaper proposal pays for equipment only.

script.speaker: Panel member
script.text: Are you saying the cheaper option has no benefits?

script.speaker: Applicant
script.text: Not at all. It might be suitable for a short project, but our training could help people maintain equipment afterwards.

script.speaker: Panel member
script.text: Can you guarantee volunteers will remain available?

script.speaker: Applicant
script.text: No. We have expressions of interest, not commitments, so the budget includes a review before the second year.

questions.prompt: What additional feature does the applicant’s proposal include?

options.text: A guarantee of permanent volunteer availability

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 較昂貴的方案包括培訓本地義工。

questions.prompt: How does the applicant characterise the cheaper option?

options.text: It may suit a shorter project despite having a different scope
It includes the same training at a lower price

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 申請者承認較便宜方案可能適合短期項目，但內容不同。

questions.prompt: Why is there a review before the second year?

options.text: The training is certain to remove the need for later maintenance
The cheaper proposal has already secured all the same volunteers
Volunteer interest does not guarantee future commitment

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 目前只有義工表達興趣，未有承諾，因此需要檢討。

script.speaker: Mira
script.text: The visitor centre sent us a timetable showing the last ferry at six, but the operator’s website now says five thirty.

script.speaker: Cal
script.text: The centre’s leaflet was printed in spring. The website may reflect the autumn schedule.

script.speaker: Mira
script.text: The crossing takes twenty minutes, and the coach leaves the mainland harbour at six fifteen. The six o’clock ferry arrives too late.

script.speaker: Cal
script.text: Let us telephone the operator to confirm the date and ask where passengers should wait.

script.speaker: Mira
script.text: If five thirty is correct, we can leave the museum earlier and buy food at the harbour.

script.speaker: Cal
script.text: Good. I will tell the rest of the group after we have confirmation, so nobody relies on an outdated leaflet.

questions.prompt: Why might the two ferry times differ?

options.text: One source may show a newer seasonal timetable
The coach company operates the ferry
Both sources refer to the same printed leaflet

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 旅客中心的單張較早印製，網站可能已更新秋季時間表。

questions.prompt: What would they change if the earlier ferry is confirmed?

options.text: Take a coach before visiting the museum
Assume the ferry will wait until six
Leave the museum earlier and buy food at the harbour

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 如果確認五時半開船，他們會提早離開博物館並在港口買食物。

questions.prompt: Why will Cal wait before informing the group?

options.text: The group has decided not to travel
He wants the operator to confirm the current arrangements
He plans to hide the earlier sailing

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Cal 想先向營辦商確認，避免大家依賴過時單張。

script.speaker: Jenna
script.text: The exhibition panels arrived today, but the stands listed on the delivery note are missing.

script.speaker: Noor
script.text: The supplier emailed yesterday to say the stands would travel separately and should arrive tomorrow morning.

script.speaker: Jenna
script.text: That helps. Our volunteers start arranging the display at noon, so there may still be enough time.

script.speaker: Noor
script.text: The email asks us to call by ten if the second delivery has not arrived, rather than waiting until noon.

script.speaker: Jenna
script.text: I will put a reminder in the diary and tell the volunteers that the start time is not yet guaranteed.

script.speaker: Noor
script.text: Please also keep the panels dry while we wait; the note says the printed surfaces can mark easily.

questions.prompt: Why are the stands absent from today’s delivery?

options.text: They were removed permanently from the order
The volunteers have already collected them
They were sent separately and are expected tomorrow

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 供應商電郵說明支架分開運送，預計明早送到。

questions.prompt: When should they contact the supplier if the stands do not arrive?

options.text: Tomorrow at noon, when volunteers begin setting up
After the volunteers have finished at noon

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 電郵要求若未收到，應在明早十時前致電。

questions.prompt: Why will Jenna avoid promising the volunteers a definite start?

options.text: The stands have not yet arrived
The panels are already damaged beyond use

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 支架尚未送達，所以中午能否開始仍未確定。

script.speaker: Anil
script.text: I registered for the bicycle maintenance workshop because the poster said ten pounds, but my confirmation asks for fifteen.

script.speaker: Beth
script.text: The organiser’s latest message says the poster omitted the materials charge, and apologises for the mistake.

script.speaker: Anil
script.text: Does everyone have to pay the extra five, even if they booked before the correction?

script.speaker: Beth
script.text: The message offers early bookers a choice: pay the revised total or cancel for a full refund by Friday.

script.speaker: Anil
script.text: I would still like to go, but I will check whether the total includes a basic repair kit to take home.

script.speaker: Beth
script.text: That is sensible. Reply before Friday if you decide to cancel, and keep the confirmation until the fee is clear.

questions.prompt: Why is the confirmation amount higher than the poster?

options.text: Anil booked two places by mistake
The original poster omitted a materials charge
The organiser added a late-booking penalty

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 原海報漏列材料費，因此確認信的總額較高。

questions.prompt: What choice is offered to early bookers?

options.text: Accept the revised price or cancel for a full refund by Friday
Pay immediately with no possibility of cancellation
Attend free without contacting the organiser

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 早期報名者可接受新總額，或在星期五前取消並取回全額退款。

questions.prompt: What does Anil still need to clarify?

options.text: Whether the materials charge replaces the original booking fee
Whether the refund can still be requested after Friday
Whether a basic repair kit is included

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Anil 想確認總費用是否包括可帶回家的基本維修工具包。

script.speaker: Lara
script.text: The adult learning centre emailed our spring timetable, but the attachment still has the autumn dates at the top.

script.speaker: Toby
script.text: The message says rooms are unchanged. Does it actually confirm that the class dates are the same too?

script.speaker: Lara
script.text: No, it only mentions rooms. The booking page shows a later starting week, though the tutor has not replied yet.

script.speaker: Toby
script.text: Then let us ask the centre which document has the confirmed dates before we send a reminder.

script.speaker: Lara
script.text: I can draft it now, but I will leave the first date blank until we hear back.

script.speaker: Toby
script.text: Good. We can explain the discrepancy if anyone asks, without presenting a plausible date as a confirmed one.

questions.prompt: Why does the email fail to resolve the date discrepancy?

options.text: It confirms the rooms but does not confirm the class dates
It explicitly cancels the spring course
It says the attachment contains the final corrected timetable

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 電郵只確認課室不變，未確認上課日期，故未能解決日期不一致。

questions.prompt: What will Lara do while awaiting a reply?

options.text: Send the autumn date to the whole class
Delete the booking page from the centre’s website
Draft a reminder without filling in the first date

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Lara 會先起草提示訊息，待確認後才填入首課日期。

questions.prompt: Which response best follows Toby’s advice if a student asks now?

options.text: The class will use the autumn dates because the rooms are unchanged
The documents differ, and we are checking the first date with the centre
The later date must be correct because it is on a website

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Toby 建議如實說明資料有出入，待中心確認，而不要把合理猜測當作定案。

script.speaker: Rosa
script.text: The choir’s message says the rehearsal has moved from Room Two to the upstairs hall because of a leak.

script.speaker: Ken
script.text: The hall is larger, but one member uses a wheelchair. Is the lift available this evening?

script.speaker: Rosa
script.text: The caretaker says it is working today, though the building closes at nine instead of the usual ten.

script.speaker: Ken
script.text: Then we should finish early enough to put the chairs away before closing.

script.speaker: Rosa
script.text: I will update the group now, including the lift information and the earlier finishing time.

script.speaker: Ken
script.text: Please ask people to reply if they need help getting in, so we can arrange it before they arrive.

questions.prompt: Why has the rehearsal moved?

options.text: The choir has permanently left the building
The upstairs hall is the only room with chairs
There is a leak in the original room

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 原來的二號房有漏水，因此排練改到樓上大廳。

questions.prompt: How does the earlier building closure affect the plan?

options.text: The lift will necessarily stop working immediately
The choir must allow time to put away chairs before nine
The rehearsal can continue until ten as usual

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 建築九時關門，因此要提早結束並留時間收拾椅子。

questions.prompt: Why does Ken ask members to reply about access?

options.text: Support can be arranged before they arrive
The caretaker can decide whether the rehearsal needs to move again
A larger hall automatically provides suitable access for everyone

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 先確認成員的進出需要，便可在他們到達前安排協助。
